title: dict.items()
summary: A live view of (key, value) pairs — the idiomatic way to iterate a dict.
description: A *view*, not a copy: it reflects later changes to the dict and costs O(1) to create. That is also why mutating the dict while iterating a view raises.

raises.when: The dict changes size during iteration.

examples.title: Unpack in the for target
Mutating during iteration
examples.output: RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration

real_world_usage: Rendering a mapping into a report, inverting a dict, and building sorted output from an aggregation.

common_mistakes.mistake: for k in d: v = d[k]
common_mistakes.fix: That is a second lookup per key. Use .items().

common_mistakes.mistake: Adding or removing keys while iterating
common_mistakes.fix: Iterate over list(d.items()) if you must change the dict.
It is a view — no indexing. Wrap in list() if you need that.

performance_notes: O(1) to create, O(n) to iterate, no copy. `list(d.items())` does copy and is O(n) memory.
